about: 23 canonical behavioral questions, deduplicated from 30 commonly reported interview prompts. Company-specific prompts (e.g. 'Why do you want to work at <Company>?') are excluded because they can't be answered from your history alone; add them as custom questions with company context if you need them.
removed_as_company_specific: Why do you want to work at Google?

questions.question: Tell me about yourself.
questions.assesses: A concise, relevant career narrative; communication; whether your path leads naturally to this role.
questions.look_for: Current role and scope, the through-line across roles, 2-3 strongest outcomes with numbers, what you want next (from motivation notes).

questions.question: Tell me about a time you solved a complex or difficult problem. How did you go about it?
variants: Tell me about a time when you solved a complex problem and how you went about it.
Tell me about a time when you had to solve a difficult problem.
questions.assesses: Structured problem solving: framing, decomposition, hypotheses, persistence, judgment.
questions.look_for: Investigations, ambiguous problems, root-cause analyses, multi-step debugging or analysis where your reasoning is documented.

questions.question: Tell me about a technical challenge you overcame.
variants: Tell me about a technical challenge that you have overcome.
questions.assesses: Technical depth, tradeoff reasoning, ownership of a hard technical outcome.
questions.look_for: Design docs/RFCs, migrations, performance or reliability work, incidents you resolved; options considered and why one won.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you solved a problem in an innovative way.
variants: Tell me about a time when you solved a problem innovatively.
questions.assesses: Creativity, challenging assumptions, simplifying, finding a non-obvious approach.
questions.look_for: Reframed problems, tools or automation you built, process changes, unusual approaches that beat the obvious one.

questions.question: What is the most challenging situation you've faced in your career, and how did you handle it?
variants: Tell me about the most challenging situation you faced in your career and how you handled it.
questions.assesses: Resilience, composure and judgment under pressure; the scale of challenge you can handle.
questions.look_for: Crises, turnarounds, reorgs, major incidents, high-stakes launches, situations your journal shows were hard.

questions.question: What is the project you are most proud of?
questions.assesses: What you value, depth of ownership, impact, how you talk about your own work.
questions.look_for: High-impact work with a clearly personal contribution and some growth or difficulty; brag docs and self-reviews.

questions.question: Tell me about the most complex project you have led.
questions.assesses: Leadership of scope: planning, coordination across people and teams, risk management, execution.
questions.look_for: Multi-team or multi-quarter projects you drove: plans, dependencies, launch docs, status updates, how you kept it on track.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you made a short-term sacrifice for long-term gain.
variants: Tell me about a time when you made short-term sacrifices for long-term gains.
questions.assesses: Long-term thinking, ownership, judgment about tradeoffs.
questions.look_for: Tech-debt paydown, declining a quick hack, investing in tooling or tests, delaying a launch, giving up scope or credit; the measured payoff.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you made a decision with limited data or took a calculated risk when speed was critical.
variants: Tell me about a time you took a calculated risk when speed was critical.
Tell me about a time when you made a decision with limited data.
questions.assesses: Bias for action, reasoning under uncertainty, limiting downside (reversibility, rollback, staged rollout).
questions.look_for: Decisions under time pressure or incomplete information, experiments, two-way-door calls, rollback plans.

questions.question: How do you prioritize your work? For example, if you had five projects at once, how would you decide?
variants: How do you prioritize tasks?
If you had to work on five different projects, how would you prioritize them?
questions.assesses: A real prioritization method, impact vs. effort thinking, communicating tradeoffs, saying no.
questions.look_for: Planning docs, OKRs, triage notes, explicit deprioritizations and how you communicated them.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you dealt with conflicting priorities between stakeholders. How did you get alignment?
variants: Tell me about a time when you had to deal with conflicting priorities with your stakeholders and how you secured alignment with them.
questions.assesses: Influence without authority, negotiation, framing tradeoffs, driving to a decision.
questions.look_for: Roadmap conflicts, competing asks from teams or leaders, escalations, decision meetings you ran.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you worked on a project with a tight deadline.
variants: Tell me about a time when you worked on a project with a tight deadline.
questions.assesses: Planning and scoping under pressure, focus, quality tradeoffs, keeping people informed.
questions.look_for: Launches against fixed dates (regulatory, contractual, events), scope cuts, crunch plans, retros.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you missed a deadline.
variants: Tell me about a time when you missed a deadline.
questions.assesses: Ownership, raising risk early, recovery, what you changed afterward.
questions.look_for: Slips, re-plans, delayed launches; feedback about late risk flagging; retros.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you made a mistake or failed. What would you do differently?
variants: Tell me about a time you made a mistake.
Tell me about a time you failed. What would you have done differently?
questions.assesses: Self-awareness, ownership without excuses, learning, systemic fixes.
questions.look_for: Postmortems where you caused or contributed to the problem, wrong bets, action items you drove afterward.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you received negative feedback. How did you handle it?
variants: Tell me about a time when you received negative feedback and how you handled it.
questions.assesses: Coachability, emotional maturity, concrete behavior change.
questions.look_for: Performance reviews, 1:1 notes, peer feedback with criticism, and later evidence that you changed.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had a conflict or disagreement with someone. How did you resolve it, and what did you learn?
variants: Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone and how you resolved it.
Tell me about a time you had a conflict with someone. How did you resolve it and what did you learn?
Can you provide an example of how you manage conflict?
questions.assesses: Empathy, listening, using data, finding resolution while keeping the relationship.
questions.look_for: Design debates, disagreements recorded in docs or 1:1 notes, compromises, disagree-and-commit moments.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager.
variants: Tell me about a time when you had a disagreement with your manager.
questions.assesses: Courage to push back respectfully, reasoning with evidence, disagree-and-commit.
questions.look_for: 1:1 notes, proposals that countered a manager's plan, escalations, outcomes.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult person at work.
variants: Tell me about a time when you dealt with a difficult person at work.
questions.assesses: Professionalism, empathy, boundary-setting, keeping focus on the outcome.
questions.look_for: Recurring friction in journal or 1:1 notes, how you changed the working relationship, results.

questions.question: Describe an experience working on a cross-functional team.
variants: Describe an experience working in a cross-functional team.
questions.assesses: Collaboration across disciplines, shared goals, translating between functions.
questions.look_for: Projects with product, design, data, sales, legal, compliance or operations partners; your role in bridging them.

questions.question: How do you earn the trust of your team members?
questions.assesses: Reliability, transparency, care for others, following through.
questions.look_for: Joining a new team, mentoring, owning mistakes openly, keeping commitments, feedback that mentions trust.

questions.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
questions.assesses: Self-awareness backed by evidence; honesty about a real weakness and what you're doing about it.
questions.look_for: Praise that recurs across reviews (strengths), criticism that recurs (weakness), and steps you've taken since.

questions.question: Why should we not hire you?
variants: Why do you think we should not hire you?
questions.assesses: Honesty and composure; awareness of genuine gaps relative to the role and how you mitigate them.
questions.look_for: Real gaps versus the target role, working-style preferences, growth areas from reviews, mitigation already underway.

questions.question: Why do you want to switch jobs now?
questions.assesses: Positive, forward-looking motivation that fits your career arc; no badmouthing.
questions.look_for: Career-planning notes, journal reflections about what energizes you and what you want next; confirm with the person.
